core.big_idea: New Testament elders are described through character, teaching ability, household credibility, and shepherding responsibility.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic churches: Leadership within the Church, Worship, and Mission cycle

claims.statement: Paul summons the Ephesian elders and describes their responsibility to watch themselves and shepherd the flock.
1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1 emphasize character, household credibility, self-control, hospitality, and ability to teach among elder qualifications.
Across these passages, New Testament oversight is characterized by qualified character, teaching responsibility, and shepherding rather than status or celebrity.
Within this curriculum framework, the elder/overseer office is reserved for qualified men while women serve broadly in other ministries.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The masculine qualification language, household requirements, and wider New Testament synthesis are read together as restricting the elder office while not restricting women from broad Christian service.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that new testament elders are described through character, teaching ability, household credibility, and shepherding responsibility.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
